question: In a circle, two chords, AB and CD, measuring 14 cm and 6 cm, respectively, are parallel to each other on the same side of the centre. If the distance between them is 4 cm, find the length (in cm) of the diameter of the circle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let half-chords be **a = 7 cm** and **b = 3 cm**, and distance between them **d = 4 cm**.

Distance of the longer chord from the center **x = (a² − b² − d²) ÷ (2d)**.

⇒ x = (7² − 3² − 4²) ÷ (2 × 4) = (49 − 9 − 16) ÷ 8 = **3 cm**.

Radius **r = √(x² + a²)** = √(3² + 7²) = √(9 + 49) = **√58 cm**.

Diameter = 2 × r = **2√58 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2√58 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Chords **AB = 14 cm**, **CD = 6 cm**, and distance between them **MN = 4 cm**.

**Formula Used:** In a circle, **r² = (chord/2)² + (distance from center)²**.
